findings.limitation: The design may intentionally delegate execution to an external verifier. The integration that executes tests and produces a trustworthy receipt must be separately wired and audited.
findings.statement: The controller exposes verification/iteration gate APIs and validates a supplied verification record. No test-runner or subprocess execution call was observed inside AE-29. Consequently, a valid verification receipt can be checked for consistency and binding, but this component alone does not execute the tests that generated it.
findings.title: AE-29 validates verification evidence but does not run the verification tests itself

findings.limitation: A fixed allowlist is a legitimate security boundary for a narrow diagnostic. The gap is the absence of a safe, queryable evidence-selection tool within that boundary, not the existence of a boundary itself.
findings.statement: The diagnosis component declares explicit input/context path lists and no graph-query API was observed in that component. This limits discovery to files selected in advance instead of following dependencies from the current failure.
findings.title: LLM diagnosis context is assembled from a fixed file allowlist

findings.limitation: Indirect use through an external process or runtime wrapper is not visible to static source analysis.
findings.statement: The repository contains consumers of SemanticGraphAnalysisService, but none of the detected LLM-requesting AE components shows direct graph-query evidence. The graph and LLM capabilities therefore appear adjacent rather than integrated in the audited source path.
findings.title: Graph analysis is used elsewhere but not in the detected LLM request path

findings.limitation: This is a source-level observation; it does not establish that the provider call fails or that no external wrapper supplies additional context.
findings.statement: Static inspection found a model-provider HTTP call but no graph-query API use or explicit model tool-dispatch loop in this component. If the intended behavior is interactive repository investigation, the model currently appears to receive preassembled context rather than request graph-grounded tools.
findings.title: ae31 makes LLM requests without observed graph/tool integration

findings.limitation: Detection is heuristic and may miss a tool loop implemented through an indirect or differently named abstraction.
findings.statement: The scanned Python source did not expose both a detectable model tool-call protocol and a corresponding tool-dispatch mechanism. Provider HTTP calls alone are not equivalent to an LLM that can request repository inspection tools over multiple turns.
findings.title: No explicit LLM tool-use loop was observed

findings.limitation: This is an intentional adapter boundary if a separate orchestrator supplies model output; the missing capability is the orchestration path, not necessarily AE-28 itself.
findings.statement: The component exposes model-response intake/validation functions, but no direct provider transport was observed in AE-28. It is a boundary for validating an output supplied by another caller, not a model invocation or interactive tool loop by itself.
findings.title: AE-28 validates externally supplied model output but does not call an LLM provider

findings.limitation: The two memory implementations may intentionally serve different purposes; this report does not assume they should be merged.
findings.statement: AE-29 defines and uses a bounded in-memory DecisionMemory type, while the repository also contains a separate decision_memory package. No import bridge from AE-29 to that package was observed in the scanned source. Cross-run reuse through the shared package is therefore not established by this path.
findings.title: AE-29 local DecisionMemory is not wired to the separate decision_memory package

findings.limitation: Indirect or generated test coverage may not be detected by static references.
findings.statement: The scanner found implementation files but no test file that directly imports or references this component. This is a coverage signal, not proof that the code is untested through another path.
findings.title: No direct test reference was observed for ae14

findings.limitation: A dedicated report-only diagnostic may intentionally require different limits or endpoints; the finding recommends reviewing the boundary, not blindly replacing it.
findings.statement: The repository has a shared provider factory used by the FEA entrypoint, while the detected AE-31 LLM requests are implemented directly in the diagnosis module. This duplicates provider transport/configuration paths and makes common retry, telemetry, and adapter behavior harder to reuse.
findings.title: AE-31 uses direct provider HTTP transport rather than the shared provider factory

findings.limitation: The report does not infer the result of any live-provider run from synthetic tests.
findings.statement: The evaluator contains expected/actual case outcomes but no live model transport. This supports control-loop transition testing, not a claim that a live LLM can find real repository defects or produce correct patches.
findings.title: AE-30 evaluation evidence is synthetic control-loop evaluation, not live diagnosis qualification

findings.limitation: The audit covers only workflow files present in the supplied source tree. A workflow stored only on another branch is outside this scan.
findings.statement: The scanned GitHub workflow commands invoke application entrypoints and validation tools, but no command directly invokes an audit_engine.semantic_audit.aeNN module. Component tests and a module CLI do not by themselves establish an operational repository-audit workflow.
findings.title: No workflow invocation of an AE package CLI was observed in the scanned tree
